reviewMethod: Independent visual reading of all 32 question-paper pages and PDF pages 3–43 of the combined Higher Level scheme (general notes, the Paper 1 scale table on page 6, and every Paper 1 model solution and marking note). Each task boundary is the published scale, not a parser count.
sourceNotes: Candidates answer any five of Q1–6 (30 marks each) and any three of Q7–10 (50 marks each): 380 offered marks, 300 candidate marks. Every question is retained; no combined multi-question cards.
42 independently marked units. Shared scales keep their parts together: Q5(b)(i)–(ii) 10D, Q8(e)(i)–(ii) 5D, Q9(a)–(b) 10D, Q10(a)(i)–(ii) 10C, Q10(b)(i)–(ii) 5C and Q10(f)(i)–(ii) 15D.
The question booklet is LC003ALP100EV.pdf; its indexed scheme LC003ALP000EV.pdf is shared with Paper 2. All page references are PDF positions.
Q1(c) Method 4 continues on scheme page 9 and Q5(b)’s completed Venn diagram is on page 20; both pages are attached to those tasks.
Diagrams (Venn diagram, cylinder, graphs of g, h, f and f′) are read from the attached original question pages; prompts quote the paper’s own wording.

Some scheme text layers mis-map bold digits (for example P(7) prints as a doubled digit), so card rows quote only notes whose text layer matches the printed scheme; the scheme reader shows the full published notes.

cards.stem: As part of her training, Ella also lifts weights. The number of times in a row that she can lift any given weight is called the number of reps that she can do with that weight. There are different formulas that Ella can use to estimate the heaviest weight that she could lift just once, called her one-repetition maximum (M). Two of these formulas are shown below. Each formula gives a value for M in kg, using the fact that Ella can do r reps with a weight of w kg. Epley formula: M = w × (1 + r/30). Brzycki formula: M = w × (36/(37 − r)).
